payload.blocks: Phases 1 and 2 of plan 261127-1535 (wave 1), and through them phases 3-5. Nothing else.
payload.headline: Plan-claim wave 1: every unit dies at the runner's output-limit on the thehive seat; which seat runs it?

parts.cause: The deepseek seat explores these large Rust files (land.rs and git refs) by dumping them whole, and the runner stops a run whose stdout capture reaches its cap. The lead cannot pin a provider (only a human --override pins), and a fourth identical run would fail the same way.

options.does: You (or the supervisor on your word) run the two phases with --override to a claude or codex seat; the lead reviews and lands as usual.
options.gain: Most likely to finish; these phases need careful reasoning about push outcomes.
options.label: A. Owner pins a stronger seat

options.cost: A config change, then two more runs of about 15 minutes.
options.does: Raise the runner output cap in config, then the lead reruns on the same seat.
options.harm: The flash seat may still not finish the reasoning; the config change is outside this plan.
options.label: B. Raise the stdout capture cap

options.does: Nothing runs until the seat pool changes.
options.harm: The admission-stranding bug stays open on every machine.
options.label: C. Leave parked

parts.recommendation: A: pin a claude or codex seat for phases 1 and 2.

scope.allows: Running phases 1 and 2 of this plan on the chosen seat, inside the plan's footprint.
scope.forbids: Changing the plan's scope, footprint or acceptance criteria.

parts.what: Three code:implement units (phase 1 once, phase 2 twice) were decided to executor gemini, but the run took the thehive/deepseek-v4.1-flash seat. Each ran 11-17 minutes, filled about 10 MB of captured stdout, and settled execution-failure with runner note output-limit. No file changed in either worktree.
